newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian central bank leaves rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Colombian central bank leaves rates unchanged.

text.p: Colombia's central bank left interest rates unchanged Friday after a meeting of its policy- making board of directors.
"There was no decision about a reduction in rates," a bank spokesman said.

He conceded that board members discussed Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo's call for a cut in rates to help boost demand to ensure a recovery from last year's sharp economic slowdown. But a majority decided that no move should be made until April inflation figures are known, the spokesman said.

Colombia's interest rates have dropped by nine percentage points over the last year. But they are still much higher than the levels seen in 1995 and 1994, when economic growth totalled 5.36 and 5.8 percent, respectively. The economy grew by just 2.08 percent in 1996.
Ocampo, who sits on the central bank's board, has insisted on a slight easing of monetary policy to help ensure a return to solid growth in 1997.
